reviewer: sdk_differentiable independent review of root SDK program/cloud adapters
conclusion: Two actionable credential-boundary findings were reproduced, fixed by the implementation owner, and independently rechecked. No open blocking finding in the reviewed paths.

focus: real SDK serialization and input/output mapping

findings.problem: Truncating nonzero-exit stderr before redaction could retain a prefix of the newly forwarded SUPERSTAQ_API_KEY when the value straddled the 2000-character boundary.
findings.fix: Redact complete stderr using the child environment before slicing the displayed error.
findings.verification: Independent runLocalJsonProcess child wrote padding and a synthetic environment value to stderr, then exited nonzero. No real credential was used.

findings.problem: Requests default trust_env could consult netrc and replace the explicitly configured API key with unrelated Basic credentials. Even allow_redirects=False can prepare response.next, which consults the redirect target netrc.
findings.fix: An explicit AuthBase always sets Authorization to the configured key. OfficialSession.resolve_redirects yields no next request; request rejects 3xx while trust_env remains enabled for user proxy and CA handling.
findings.verification: Normal requests used a patched Session.send and get_netrc_auth that raises. Redirect checks patched HTTPAdapter.send, retained real Requests request preparation, and made any get_netrc_auth access fail. Proxy/CA observations apply at the Python session boundary; the shared worker environment retains its own explicit allowlist. The final MCP contract regression additionally confirms REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE survives the controlled worker environment boundary.

independentlyExecutedExistingTests.scope: Schema rejection, protocol fixtures, named credential forwarding and error redaction. Fixture workers are not claimed as numerical SDK evidence.
Actual qiskit-ionq local serialization, gate encodings, radians, terminal measurements, idle qubits and reversed controls.
Actual qiskit-superstaq request/response and QPY mapping with local HTTP transport mocks; includes the final lower-level redirect/netrc regression.

additionalIndependentChecks.errorTruncation: Synthetic credential straddling the display boundary no longer leaks a prefix.
additionalIndependentChecks.credentialPolicy: Only the trusted Superstaq entrypoint names SUPERSTAQ_API_KEY; requests cannot supply credential names, values, URLs or endpoints. Another synthetic provider key was not forwarded.
additionalIndependentChecks.termsBoundary: 401 is intercepted before upstream interactive account/terms behavior; 3xx is rejected before SDK handling.
additionalIndependentChecks.submissionBoundary: Source and SDK call paths use serialization, targets and compilation only; no backend.run, job creation, shots or QPU submission surface is exposed.
additionalIndependentChecks.diffWhitespaceCheck: git diff --check passed after the reviewed fixes.
additionalIndependentChecks.workerProtocolCompatibility: Final increment sends toolName only for multiple-definition servers; the SDK-cloud contracts were rerun after this increment: four passed, zero failed/skipped.

requestsCaBundleRuntimeCheck.transport: actual MCP stdio and controlled local worker fixture

caWorkerEnvironment.curlCaBundleCheck: Source review confirms the same explicit environment allowlist forwarding path; no separate runtime assertion was added.
caWorkerEnvironment.commentReview: The stdio contract comment now covers both single-action and multi-action servers without implying that every action is local.

boundaries: Actual installed SDK code was used; external HTTP was mocked and Python socket connection entry points were denied in the SDK tests.
No real API credential, cloud account, cloud compiler, billing operation, external model or QPU was exercised.
The node SDK-cloud live MCP suite was inspected, but its implementation-owner execution is not counted as this reviewer independent run.

Proxy and CA preservation was checked directly on the Python session; a subsequent actual MCP/controlled-worker regression verifies that REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE reaches both SDK worker environments. CURL_CA_BUNDLE forwarding was reviewed in the same explicit allowlist. No real TLS exchange was attempted.
These are engineering and local SDK mapping checks on macOS arm64, not scientific Acceptance or remote-service availability evidence.
